description:
Plan (research + design, no build yet): an all-day wearable that collects hand-manipulation data, something Jake would be excited to wear every day, so he can match the big labs on data volume. Core idea: a watch or wristband with a wrist camera (plus hand pose from the camera, or a light glove) that keeps a rolling buffer recording locally and discards it unless Jake triggers a save with a gesture, e.g. the Spider-Man sign or pointing. On trigger, keep the last N seconds plus the next M seconds as a labeled episode. Cover:
- Hardware options and cost: off-the-shelf wrist cams (Insta360/GoPro wrist mounts), smartwatch-based, a custom ESP32-S3/XIAO camera band, glove sensors.
- Battery life for all-day wear, storage, and how the data syncs to the Mac.
- Gesture detection on-device.
- Privacy: nothing leaves the buffer untriggered; bystanders.
- How the episodes become training data for the Aero Hand plus reBot (LeRobot format, retargeting to the hand), and whether to pair it with the human-mirror eye-height cameras (e.g. a head or glasses cam).
- What makes it useful enough to wear daily beyond data.
- Prior art: UMI gripper, DexCap, Generalist, Meta Aria, egocentric datasets.
Deliver a plan doc in plans/ with a recommended first prototype.

results.identified_issue: Plan-only turn. Key assumptions to re-check before buying: XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense draws ~154 mA@3.8V streaming (Seeed/retailer figure, not measured); OV2640 vs OV3660 module detail is unverified for WiLoR/HaMeR; watchOS handGestureShortcut double-tap availability for third-party actions depends on Watch model (Series 9/Ultra 2+). Conflict with plans/hand_1_0.md 'mirror a human' (no wrist cams) resolved by assuming option A (wrist cam = action labels, eye-height cam = observations) — Jake has not confirmed. Rejected: Insta360 GO 3S / GoPro HindSight (runtime 38-140 min, button-only, no API), camera smartwatches (closed), all-day gloves (not wearable daily), all-day head cam buffer (privacy + battery). Prior-art rows for UMI, DexCap, Aria, EgoMimic, Digits were written from memory, not re-verified. The app picks up plans/*.md via Scripts/stage_plans.py, so no registration was needed.
results.summary: Wrote plans/wrist_wearable.md: a plan for Wristlog, a camera pod on your Apple Watch strap that keeps a 60-second buffer and saves an episode when you double-tap.
results.detailed_description:
The recommended first prototype is a ~$40 XIAO ESP32-S3 camera pod clipped to your Watch band and aimed at your fingers. It overwrites a 60 s ring buffer on microSD and saves the last 20 s plus the next 20 s when the Watch's double-tap pinch fires. You get a haptic tap and an optional label, and it syncs to the Mac on the charger. The Spider-Man sign becomes the v1 trigger, trained on v0's own clips, because running a vision detector all day costs battery and its false-trigger rate is unknown. No audio, ever.

Battery is the real limit: a wrist camera draws ~0.6 W, so a 1000 mAh cell gives ~5 h. Getting to all day means the Watch tells the pod to sleep while your hands are still. Insta360 and GoPro have pre-record buffers but last 40–140 min with no custom trigger, so they lose.

One decision for you: your mirror-a-human rule says no wrist cameras. The plan treats the wrist camera as a finger-pose sensor (labels for retargeting to the Aero Hand's 7 actuations) and adds an eye-height camera in v1 for what the robot sees. Say if you'd rather put a wrist camera on the robot instead. To be honest about volume: ~1 h/day won't match the labs, so grab EgoDex (829 h, free) for pretraining. The first build step is one evening of wearing the pod to see whether your fingers stay in frame.

results.notes: Jake: once the plan picks a first prototype, mock the wearable up in 3D (OpenSCAD, his preference) and add it as a project on the Helping Hands Designs page with its render.

user_request.name: I want to wear a camera and something on my hands all day long, every day... a wrist camera. Maybe a watch with a wrist camera... activate it is by doing Spider-Man... Or I point and it records. Otherwise it's recording locally but not doing anything.

summary: Jake wants a research-and-design plan doc in plans/ for an all-day wrist wearable with a rolling local buffer that saves hand-manipulation episodes only on a gesture trigger. It should compare hardware, battery, sync, on-device gesture detection, privacy, and conversion to LeRobot data for the Aero Hand and reBot, and recommend a first prototype.
